public.suggestedRevision: A referance architecture serves as a technology-independent framework that delineates the fundamental components, interconnections and design principles of technical ecosystem, enabling organisations to avoid beginning from scratch. Utilising recognised enterprise architectural methodologies, it acts as a definitive referance that directs the creation of more tailored architectures and solutions, while providing an organised framework of reusable components. Its significance resides in providing various stakeholders with a unified framework - a collective terminology and organisational structure that harmonises decisions, minimises redundancy and facilitates the integration and sustainability of application components. In the context of health, where services are provided through numerous programs, institutions and tiers of care, this holds particular significance. A reference architecture offers nations a unified method to convert broad health policy objectives into digital frameworks taht are interoperable, manageable, and tailored to their specific circumstances.
